description: An analogue to digital converter: it measures the voltage at the input jack and puts the result out as up to eight parallel logic bits.

params.text: How many of the eight outputs carry the number, from 2 to 8. Outputs above the setting are held at 0V and the whole conversion range is spread across the ones that remain.
Scales the input voltage before conversion: fully clockwise passes it unchanged, fully anticlockwise gives 0V. The tooltip counts this 0 to 10.
The input voltage at which every bit in use is high, adjustable from 1V to 10V. The conversion covers 0V up to this voltage in equal steps.

inputs.text: The voltage that gets converted. It is scaled by the LEVEL knob first, then anything below 0V or above the REFERENCE voltage is clipped away.

outputs.text: The least significant bit of the converted number.
The second bit of the converted number, worth two.
The third bit of the converted number, worth four. It is held at 0V while BITS is set to 2.
The fourth bit of the converted number, worth eight. It is held at 0V while BITS is set below 4.
The fifth bit of the converted number, worth sixteen. It is held at 0V while BITS is set below 5.
The sixth bit of the converted number, worth thirty-two. It is held at 0V while BITS is set below 6.
The seventh bit of the converted number, worth sixty-four. It is held at 0V while BITS is set below 7.
The most significant bit of the converted number, worth one hundred and twenty-eight. It is held at 0V unless BITS is set to 8.

notes: A logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
The ERROR lamp comes on when the scaled input voltage goes below 0V or more than half a step above the REFERENCE voltage, which is the sign that LEVEL or REFERENCE needs changing.
The converter is free-running: it reads the input every sample and there is no clock or sample-and-hold input.

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
